activities.prompt: Read Mr Silva's restaurant visit. What did he ask for first?
activities.feedback: A table for two — 'Queria uma mesa para dois, por favor.'

activities.body: A new mood: the conjuntivo. After quero que, é preciso que and espero que, the verb changes its vowel — falas becomes fales, comes becomes comas. Find the flipped vowels in the examples: fales, estudes, venhas, tenhas. This is the grammar of wishes and hopes. Say them out loud; the -e- where you expect -a- is the sound of wanting.

activities.prompt: Which is correct after 'quero que'?
activities.feedback: Quero que fales mais devagar — the conjuntivo flips falas to fales. 'Quero que falas' uses the indicative and is wrong; falar and falava don't belong here at all.

activities.prompt: Predict the form: 'É preciso que ___ para o exame.' (you study)
activities.feedback: É preciso que estudes — -ar verbs flip -a- to -e- in the conjuntivo: estudes.

answers: É preciso que estudes para o exame.

activities.prompt: Which phrase triggers the conjuntivo?
activities.feedback: Quero que — wishing triggers the conjuntivo. Acho que, sei que and vejo que state facts, so they keep the indicative.

activities.prompt: Put the words in order: I hope you come tomorrow.
activities.feedback: Espero que venhas amanhã — espero que + conjuntivo (vir → venhas).

activities.prompt: Fill the gap: Quero que ___ mais devagar. (you speak)
activities.feedback: Fales — the conjuntivo of falar for tu: fales.

activities.prompt: Read the mother's instructions. What time must he be home?
activities.feedback: At ten — 'é preciso que chegues a casa às dez'.

activities.body: Stop making short sentences. In the examples, find the three joiners: que for things and people (o livro que comprei), com quem for a person after a preposition (a pessoa com quem falei), onde for places (a casa onde nasci). Ask yourself: place? person-after-preposition? Otherwise que. Read each sentence out loud and feel two ideas become one.

activities.prompt: Which joins correctly? 'A casa ___ nasci é pequena.'
activities.feedback: Onde — places take onde. Que would need a preposition ('em que'), and quem is for people.

options.text: A casa onde nasci é pequena.
A casa que nasci é pequena.
A casa quem nasci é pequena.
A casa com nasci é pequena.

activities.prompt: Predict the joiner: 'O livro ___ comprei é ótimo.'
activities.feedback: Que — for a thing as the object, plain que does the job.

answers: O livro que comprei é ótimo.

activities.prompt: After a preposition + person, we use…
activities.feedback: Com quem — preposition + quem for people: a pessoa com quem falei. Never 'com que' for a person.

activities.prompt: Put the words in order: The house where I was born is small.
activities.feedback: A casa onde nasci é pequena — noun, onde-clause, then the main verb.

activities.prompt: Fill the gap: O café ___ almoçamos é fixe. (where)
activities.feedback: Onde — a place takes onde.

activities.body: Time to take sides. The examples show the three frames: mais… do que, tão… como, and the rebels that change completely — melhor, pior. Notice do que (than) after mais/menos, and como (as) after tão. Say each comparison out loud; Portuguese debate runs on these frames.

activities.prompt: Which is correct? 'Este café é ___ do que o outro.'
activities.feedback: Melhor — bom becomes melhor, and it never takes mais. 'Mais melhor' and 'mais bom' do not exist.

activities.prompt: Predict the frame: 'O Porto é mais pequeno ___ Lisboa.'
activities.feedback: Do que — mais… do que is the full frame for 'than'.

answers: O Porto é mais pequeno do que Lisboa.

activities.prompt: Which means 'as tall as'?
activities.feedback: Tão alta como — tão… como is the 'as… as' frame. Mais/menos… do que compare unequal things.

activities.prompt: Say: Traffic is worse today.
activities.feedback: Hoje o trânsito está pior — mau becomes pior; estar for a temporary state.

activities.prompt: Fill the gap: Este café é ___ do que o outro. (better)
activities.feedback: Melhor — the irregular comparative of bom.

activities.prompt: Read the café debate. Why does Ana prefer the Central?
activities.feedback: It's cheaper and the service is better — 'é mais barato do que o café Roma e o atendimento é melhor'.

answers: It's cheaper and the service is better.
It is cheaper and the service is better.
É mais barato e o atendimento é melhor.

activities.prompt: Which means 'I gave her the book'?
activities.feedback: Dei-lhe o livro — lhe is the indirect object pronoun (to her). 'Dei ela' is wrong, and 'dei para ela' misses the natural habit.

activities.prompt: Predict the pronoun: 'Emprestei-___ o meu carro.' (to him)
activities.feedback: Emprestei-lhe o meu carro — -lhe attaches with a hyphen: to him/her.

activities.prompt: Which sentence places the pronoun correctly after 'não'?
activities.feedback: Não lhe disse nada — after não the pronoun goes before the verb. 'Não disse-lhe' breaks the rule.

activities.prompt: Say: I didn't tell him anything.
activities.feedback: Não lhe disse nada — não pulls the pronoun before the verb.

activities.prompt: Fill the gap: Disse-___ a verdade. (to her)
activities.feedback: Lhe — disse-lhe: told her.

activities.prompt: Which is correct? 'Vens ___ ao cinema?'
activities.feedback: Comigo — com + mim fuses into comigo. 'Com eu' is never correct, and para mim means 'for me', not 'with me'.

activities.prompt: Predict the form: 'Este café é ___ .' (for me)
activities.feedback: Para mim — after para, eu becomes mim.

activities.prompt: Which pair is correct after a preposition?
activities.feedback: Para ti — prepositions take mim/ti, never eu/tu. 'Para tu' is the giveaway error.

activities.prompt: Say: This present is for you.
activities.feedback: Este presente é para ti — para + ti.

activities.prompt: Fill the gap: Vens ___ ao cinema? (with me)
activities.feedback: Comigo — the fused form of com + mim.

activities.prompt: Read Joana's invitation. How many tickets does she have?
activities.feedback: Two — 'Tenho dois bilhetes — um é para mim e o outro é para ti.'

activities.body: How to praise things properly. In the examples find the two superlatives: o mais… da cidade (the -est, relative) and -íssimo (absolutely, extremely). Notice o telemóvel — the very Portuguese word for mobile phone — and a reunião, a entrevista: work words you will use for real. Say fixíssimo out loud; it should sound like enthusiasm.

activities.prompt: Which one is a superlative ('the oldest')?
activities.feedback: O mais antigo da cidade — the article o + mais makes it 'the oldest'. 'Mais antigo' alone is just comparative (older).

activities.prompt: Predict the form: 'Ela é a funcionária mais ___ .' (punctual)
activities.feedback: A funcionária mais pontual — feminine article a with the feminine noun.

answers: Ela é a funcionária mais pontual.

activities.prompt: Put the words in order: We have a meeting at nine.
activities.feedback: Temos uma reunião às nove — ter + noun is the habit for 'have a meeting'.

activities.prompt: Say: My boss is really great.
activities.feedback: O meu chefe é fixíssimo — or 'A minha chefe é fixíssima' for a female boss.

activities.prompt: Fill the gap: O computador novo é ___ . (super fast)
activities.feedback: Rapidíssimo — the -íssimo absolute superlative of rápido.

activities.prompt: Read about Sofia's new job. What time was the first meeting?
activities.feedback: At nine — 'A primeira reunião foi às nove'.

activities.body: Your mission: it's 6 in the evening in Porto and you have a reservation. Walk up to the receção, greet with 'Boa tarde', and run the script: Queria fazer o check-in, por favor. Tenho uma reserva em nome de Silva. Then ask the two questions that matter: A que horas é o pequeno-almoço? Onde fica a receção? Four sentences — read each out loud once, then walk in.

activities.prompt: You reach the desk. Which opens the check-in?
activities.feedback: Queria fazer o check-in, por favor — queria softens the request; the other options skip the check-in entirely or are blunt.

options.text: Queria fazer o check-in, por favor.

activities.prompt: State your reservation: 'I have a reservation under the name Silva.'
activities.feedback: Tenho uma reserva em nome de Silva — em nome de = under the name of.

answers: Tenho uma reserva em nome de Silva.

activities.prompt: Ask the key question: what time is breakfast?
activities.feedback: A que horas é o pequeno-almoço? — a que horas asks for a time.

activities.prompt: The receptionist asks for your booking. Complete: 'Tenho uma ___ em nome de Silva.'
activities.feedback: Reserva — a reserva, the reservation.

activities.prompt: She hands you something and says 'Aqui está a chave.' What do you get?
activities.feedback: A chave — the room key. O quarto is the room itself, a reserva the booking.

activities.prompt: Predict before you ask: what time is breakfast?
activities.feedback: A que horas é o pequeno-almoço? — say it before you need it.

answers: A que horas é o pequeno-almoço?

activities.prompt: Quick check — match each line to its meaning.
activities.feedback: Four for four. You're ready for the desk.

left.text: A que horas é o pequeno-almoço?

activities.prompt: Final run-through. Say it all: 'I'd like to check in, please.'
activities.feedback: Queria fazer o check-in, por favor — the whole mission in one sentence.

answers: Queria fazer o check-in, por favor.

activities.body: Review mission: one morning at the café, using everything from A1. You walk in (olá), order politely (queria um café, por favor), chat about yesterday (ontem fui…) and tomorrow (amanhã vou…), and leave warmly (obrigado, até amanhã). Four scenes below — read each out loud, then prove you own them.

activities.prompt: You walk into the café in the morning. What do you say?
activities.feedback: Bom dia — the morning greeting. Boa noite is for night, and a bare 'café!' skips the greeting entirely.

activities.prompt: Order politely: 'I'd like a coffee, please.'
activities.feedback: Queria um café, por favor — queria is the polite A1 habit you learned.

activities.prompt: Chat about yesterday: 'Yesterday I went to the market.'
activities.feedback: Ontem fui ao mercado — ontem + perfeito: fui.

activities.prompt: Complete the plan: 'Amanhã ___ viajar.' (I am going to)
activities.feedback: Vou — ir + infinitivo for the near future.

activities.prompt: Which declines an invitation kindly?
activities.feedback: Desta vez não posso, desculpa — the cushioned refusal from the invitations lesson. A bare 'não' sounds cold.

activities.prompt: Predict the soft refusal before you say it: 'I can't this time, sorry.'
activities.feedback: Desta vez não posso, desculpa — say it warmly.

activities.prompt: Match each line to its meaning.
activities.feedback: Six for six across the whole of A1. Bom trabalho.

activities.prompt: Leave warmly: 'Thank you! See you tomorrow.'
activities.feedback: Obrigado! Até amanhã — close every interaction the Portuguese way.

activities.prompt: Quick check — match each comparison to its meaning.
activities.feedback: Comparatives matched. Nicely done.

activities.prompt: The operator asks where you are. You need the word for ‘hospital’, fast. Which is it?
activities.feedback: O hospital — name the place first, then the street.

activities.prompt: You want the price first. What do you say?
activities.feedback: Quanto custa isto? — the price question opens every market chat.

options.feedback: Exato — the price question opens every market chat.
That's for the restaurant, at the end.
Don't call it cheap before you know the price.

activities.prompt: The shopkeeper accepts eight euros. How do you close the deal?
activities.feedback: Está bem, obrigado — accept graciously, then pay.

options.feedback: You already agreed — don't reopen the haggle.

activities.prompt: The tag says twelve euros. Which reply haggles politely?
activities.feedback: É muito caro. Faz por dez? — name the pain, then name your price.

options.text: É muito caro. Faz por dez?

activities.prompt: Your aunt points at your brother. How do you introduce him?
activities.feedback: É o meu irmão — é, the article, and the family word.

options.feedback: És is 'you are' — use é for he.

activities.prompt: Now she asks about your sister. What do you say?
activities.feedback: A minha irmã está bem, obrigada — answer the question asked.

options.text: A minha irmã está bem, obrigada.

options.feedback: True, but it doesn't answer the question.
That introduces her — she asked how she is.

activities.prompt: You have the barista's attention. Order politely.
activities.feedback: Gostaria de um café, por favor — gostaria de + por favor.

options.text: Gostaria de um café, por favor.

options.feedback: Pode needs an infinitive after it.

activities.prompt: You're done. How do you close and ask for the bill?
activities.feedback: É tudo + A conta, por favor — close the round kindly.

options.text: Não, é tudo. A conta, por favor.

options.feedback: Add the bill and the por favor.
Thanks — but you still need the bill.

activities.prompt: State your need.
activities.feedback: Preciso de aspirina, por favor — precisar + de.

options.feedback: That's a question, not a request.
One word is not a request.

activities.prompt: You have no prescription. What do you say?
activities.feedback: Não tenho receita — answer the question asked, honestly.

options.feedback: Only if it's true — it isn't.
That says you need one — answer the question.

activities.prompt: They said yes! Give a time.
activities.feedback: Às oito, está bem? — confirm the detail, keep it warm.

options.feedback: They said yes — don't uninvite them.
Close, but «está bem?» keeps it warm.

activities.prompt: You have plenty of room. What do you say?
activities.feedback: Claro que sim! — yes stays yes-shaped in Portuguese too.

options.feedback: You can ask later — answer first.

activities.prompt: Ask if they could help you.
activities.feedback: Poderia ajudar-me, por favor? — the conditional turns a demand into a request.

activities.prompt: Three nights, said as softly as possible.
activities.feedback: Seria ótimo ficar três noites — the conditional keeps the whole exchange soft.

options.feedback: Exato — the conditional keeps it soft.
A command at a front desk? Não.

activities.prompt: Put the words in order: I study Portuguese in the afternoon.
activities.feedback: Eu estudo português à tarde — subject, verb, object, time at the end.

activities.prompt: Put the words in order: Who is she?
activities.feedback: Quem é ela? — the question word leads, the rest stays put.

activities.prompt: Put the words in order: Tomorrow I'm going to travel.
activities.feedback: Amanhã vou viajar — time first, then vou + infinitive.

activities.prompt: Put the words in order: We are going to travel in August.
activities.feedback: Vamos viajar em agosto — vamos + infinitive, time at the end.

activities.prompt: Put the words in order: The book I bought is great.
activities.feedback: O livro que comprei é ótimo — que joins the clauses mid-sentence.

activities.body: No new verbs today — only memory. You learned the present in «Work and daily routine»: trabalhar, estudar, de manhã, à tarde. Yesterday’s endings attach to the stems you already own — pull them back up before you speak about ontem.

activities.prompt: Retrieve the verb: I study Portuguese in the afternoon.
activities.feedback: Eu estudo português à tarde — the -ar present you learned in «Work and daily routine».

activities.body: Your weekend story is built from retrieved verbs. You learned the finished past in «Yesterday: a first look at the past» — falei, comi, foi, fiz. Pull those four back up; the sequencers (depois, então, à noite) just need something true to carry.

activities.prompt: Retrieve the verb: Yesterday I spoke with Ana.
activities.feedback: Ontem falei com a Ana — falei, straight from «Yesterday: a first look at the past».

activities.body: Intentions stand on plans you already made. You learned the near future in «Ir + infinitivo» — vou fazer, vais sair, vamos viajar. Retrieve vou, vais, vamos first; tencionar and decidir only dress them up.

activities.prompt: Retrieve the verb: We are going to travel in August.
activities.feedback: Vamos viajar em agosto — ir + infinitive, from «Ir + infinitivo».

segments.text: viajar em agosto. (we are going to)

activities.body: Lhe and lhes hug verbs you already know. You learned the polite frames in «Polite requests» — Pode…?, Gostaria de…, por favor. Retrieve poder and gostaria de before you attach the little pronouns.

activities.prompt: Retrieve the verb: Can you help me, please?
activities.feedback: Pode ajudar-me, por favor? — poder + -me, from «Polite requests».

activities.body: Choosing the past is pure retrieval. The finished events came from «O pretérito perfeito» — falei, comeste, partiu; the habits and background from «O imperfeito» — falava, comia, era. Pull both back up — no new endings today.

activities.prompt: Retrieve the verb: Yesterday I spoke with Maria.
activities.feedback: Ontem falei com a Maria — the pretérito perfeito, from «O pretérito perfeito».

activities.body: Morning in Alfama, and you are beautifully lost. The streets tilt downhill, the trams rattle past, and your map is definitely upside down. An old man with a newspaper watches you turn in a slow circle. Onde fica a estação? — that’s your line, if you can find the courage to use it.

The old man points — em frente, depois à esquerda — and you repeat it like a spell. Two corners later the station appears, exactly where his finger promised. In Lisbon, being lost is just directions you haven’t asked for yet.

activities.prompt: The old man points left as he speaks. Which direction does «à esquerda» give you?
activities.feedback: À esquerda — left. Repeat it like a spell and walk.

activities.body: Sunday, one o’clock, and the whole family is already at the table. Avó stands over a pot that has been simmering since morning, and the smell of it follows you up the stairs. Como sopa ao almoço — today the soup is caldo verde, and there is no refusing.

After the soup comes the fish — o peixe é muito bom, avó announces, as she does every Sunday. You eat, you drink water, and when the oranges arrive you say exactly what she taught you: gosto de fruta. Some lessons come from books; this one comes from a full plate.

Saturday morning in the bairro, and everyone has a plan. Your neighbour João is already running past — jogo futebol aos sábados, he shouts over his shoulder. You have the whole day and exactly one decision: what do people do for fun here?

By afternoon you’ve tried everything: music in the park — ouço música todos os dias, says the girl with the guitar — and a long chapter under the jacaranda tree. No fim de semana descanso, you decide at last, stretching out in the sun. Rest, it turns out, is a hobby too.

February, and the flu finds you anyway. You wake with a head full of cotton — dói-me a cabeça — and a fever that makes the ceiling tilt. Tenho febre, you tell the mirror. The mirror is not sympathetic.

By noon you’re at the clinic, rehearsing your symptoms like lines: dói-me o braço from yesterday’s fall, estou doente, preciso de ajuda. The doctor nods, writes something short, and sends you home with the only prescription that matters — bed, water, and three days of doing nothing.

Yesterday started badly: you woke late, the coffee burned, and the train — ela partiu às oito, exactly on time, exactly without you. Ontem jantei em casa had been the plan; ontem corri para a estação became the reality.

What followed was a perfect pretérito perfeito of a day: falei com a Maria, comeste o bolo todo — well, you shared it — and comprámos pão de manhã as if nothing had happened. Some days you don’t live; you conjugate them.

In a blue doorway in Alfama sits Dona Lurdes, who reads the future in coffee cups for two euros. Amanhã choverá o dia todo, she announces, peering into yours — and then, because the cup demands it: no próximo ano viajarás mais.

You leave with three solemn predictions: ajudarei com as malas — your friend is moving — serei pontual, prometo, and one warning the cup was very clear about: prometer menos, cumprir mais. The future, Dona Lurdes insists, is just the present with better posture.

Mr. Silva has one perfect evening a month, and this is it. He walks into his favourite restaurant and the waiter already knows: gostaria de reservar uma mesa — done last Tuesday — and now, to open the evening, queria um café, por favor. Politeness, he believes, is a kind of music.

The evening unfolds in the conditional: seria ótimo ver-te amanhã, he tells an old friend; gostaria de falar com o gerente, to praise the cook; and at the end, the softest sentence in the language — queria a conta, por favor — settling the bill like a lullaby.

Joana is planning the party of the year and her phone never stops. «Vens comigo ao cinema?» she texts Marta — scouting the film for Saturday. «Este café é para mim?» she asks the barista, refuelling. Every message ends with a pronoun tucked after a preposition, exactly where Portuguese wants it.

The invitations go out one by one: «Quero falar contigo,» to her brother; «Posso falar consigo um minuto?» to the neighbour she barely knows; «Este presente é para ti,» on the card for her mother. By midnight the list is done — and every para, com and de is holding its pronoun like a dance partner.

lessons.title: Missão: um café em Lisboa
lessons.objective: Walk into a Lisbon pastelaria and order a coffee — your first real conversation in Portuguese.

lessons.title: Introducing yourself
lessons.objective: Introduce yourself as Ana and keep the accent that separates é ('is') from e ('and').

legacyExercises.prompt: Which question would you ask a new neighbour to learn their name in Portuguese?
legacyExercises.explanation: Qual é o seu nome? is the complete question. O meu nome é Ana answers it, and Prazer is what you say on meeting.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words back in order to give your name with O meu nome é.
legacyExercises.explanation: Keep the accent on é; it is the verb 'is', and the sentence reads as nonsense without it.

errors.explanation: Without the accent, é becomes e, 'and' — the é inside the question is the verb 'is': Qual é o seu nome?
The question keeps the little o before seu: Qual é o seu nome?

legacyExercises.prompt: Ask a neighbour's name using the full question taught here.
legacyExercises.explanation: This is the complete question, and the accent on é stays in place.

errors.explanation: European Portuguese keeps the small article o before meu: O meu nome é Ana.
é means 'is'; without the accent it becomes e, 'and' — the line would read 'my name and Ana'.

legacyExercises.prompt: Give your name as Ana with the phrase 'my name is', keeping the accent on the word for 'is'.
legacyExercises.explanation: O meu nome é Ana — the accented é is 'is'. Without the accent the word turns into 'and'.

errors.explanation: Ana's line says 'my name' (meu nome) — sou is the verb that means 'I am' on its own, and that is Leo's line.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the exchange. One speaker introduces themselves with no word for 'I' at all. Who is it?
legacyExercises.explanation: Sou Leo says 'I am Leo' with no eu; Portuguese does not need the pronoun.
legacyExercises.passage:
— Olá! O meu nome é Ana.
— Prazer, Ana. Sou Leo.
— Prazer, Leo.
legacyExercises.translation:
— Hello! My name is Ana.
— Nice to meet you, Ana. I am Leo.
— Nice to meet you, Leo.

errors.explanation: Obrigado thanks someone for a favour — at an introduction the reply is Prazer.
Olá opens the meeting — the word for 'nice to meet you' is Prazer.

legacyExercises.prompt: You have just been introduced to someone. Give the short Portuguese word meaning 'Nice to meet you'.
legacyExercises.explanation: Prazer on its own is the friendly reply at an introduction.

lessons.culturalNote: These examples use European Portuguese. Prazer is a common short greeting at an introduction. Obrigado and obrigada vary with the speaker, not with the person being thanked.

lessons.title: At the café
lessons.objective: Order with gostaria de, keeping the word that joins the verb to the drink, and match your thanks to who is speaking.

answers: Eu gostaria de um café, por favor.
legacyExercises.prompt: Only one of these keeps the little word that joins gostaria to the drink. Which is it?
legacyExercises.explanation: De belongs between gostaria and the drink; without it the request loses the link. O meu nome é Ana is an introduction, not a request.
options: Eu gostaria de um café, por favor.
Eu gostaria um café, por favor.

answers: Eu gostaria de um café, por favor.
legacyExercises.prompt: The words are out of order. Build the polite request for one coffee with gostaria de.
legacyExercises.explanation: Gostaria and the drink are held together by de, and por favor closes the request.

answers: Eu gostaria de um chá, por favor.
Gostaria de um chá, por favor.

errors.answer: Eu gostaria um chá, por favor.
errors.explanation: The de is the link between gostaria and the drink — without it the verb has nothing to join: gostaria de um chá.

errors.answer: Eu gostaria de chá, por favor.
errors.explanation: The drink keeps its um too: de um chá, not de chá.
Quero is 'I want' — this lesson practices the polite form gostaria de.

legacyExercises.prompt: Ask for tea politely, keeping the word that joins gostaria to the drink.
legacyExercises.explanation: Swap the drink but keep de: gostaria de um chá. Chá keeps its accent.

errors.answer: Eu gostaria de um café, por favor.
errors.explanation: That is the polite form with a verb — the short request leaves it out: just Um café, por favor.
Close the request with por favor — the softener that makes an order polite.

legacyExercises.prompt: At the counter you want a coffee. Make the short request, with no verb in it.
legacyExercises.explanation: Um café, por favor — the short request keeps por favor and drops gostaria.

errors.explanation: Obrigado is the man's form — the thanks agrees with the speaker, and this customer is a woman: Obrigada.
Sim is the customer's 'yes' to the server — the question asks for the thanks word, the one ending in -a.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the café exchange. The customer thanks the server. Which form of thanks tells you the customer is a woman?
legacyExercises.explanation: Obrigada, not obrigado: the word agrees with the person speaking, and this speaker is a woman.
legacyExercises.passage:
— Olá. Eu gostaria de um chá, por favor.
— Um chá?
— Sim. Obrigada!
legacyExercises.translation:
— Hello. I would like a tea, please.
— A tea?
— Yes. Thank you!

answers: I would like a coffee, please.

errors.explanation: Gostaria de is the polite 'I would like'; 'I want' would translate quero — softer language fits a shop.
English keeps the article too: a coffee, not coffee.

legacyExercises.prompt: Give the English meaning: Eu gostaria de um café, por favor.
legacyExercises.explanation: Gostaria de is 'I would like', and por favor is 'please'.

lessons.culturalNote: These café requests use European Portuguese. The lessons accept both explicit eu and its omission in the full request.

lessons.title: Numbers and quantities
lessons.objective: Count one to five, then choose between dois and duas to match the noun you are counting.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which word is three in Portuguese? Unlike two, it never changes with the noun.
legacyExercises.explanation: Três is three, and it has no masculine or feminine form to choose between.

errors.explanation: Maçã is a feminine noun, so the number takes its feminine twin: duas maçãs, not dois.
Maçã keeps its tilde — the ~ makes the nasal vowel: maçãs.
Two of them — the noun goes plural too: duas maçãs.

legacyExercises.prompt: Say in Portuguese: Two apples, please.
legacyExercises.explanation: Maçãs is feminine, so the number becomes duas. With a masculine noun such as cafés it would be dois.

errors.explanation: Name the thing being priced — um café: the um marks one masculine coffee.
Café is masculine, so the article is um — uma goes with feminine nouns.
The Portuguese question leads with Quanto: Quanto custa um café? (Custa quanto is the Brazilian ordering.)

legacyExercises.prompt: Think: you want one coffee and no price is posted. Ask in Portuguese, then write the question.
legacyExercises.explanation: Quanto custa is fixed and does not agree with anything. Say the question aloud before you check it.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the Portuguese words in order to ask the price of one coffee.
legacyExercises.explanation: Quanto custa leads, then um café names the thing being priced. Um matches the masculine café.

lessons.culturalNote: In Portugal, prices and quantities arrive quickly in ordinary errands. Hear the number first, then the item.

lessons.title: Asking the way
lessons.objective: Ask where a place stays with ficar, then walk two steps whose second one wears a grave accent.

legacyExercises.prompt: Portuguese asks where a place 'stays'. Which of these words does the asking?
legacyExercises.explanation: Onde means where. Quem is the one for a person and o que for a thing. The direction words beside it answer rather than ask.

answers: Onde fica a casa de banho?
legacyExercises.prompt: Ask in Portuguese where the bathroom is.
legacyExercises.explanation: Fica is the ficar form used for where something sits, and casa de banho is feminine, so its article is a. The question frame does not change with the noun.

legacyExercises.prompt: Complete the directions: Em frente, depois à ___
legacyExercises.explanation: Esquerda is left. The accent on à fuses the preposition a with the article a, and direita would point the other way.

legacyExercises.prompt: Soften the question by putting Desculpe in front: Onde fica a estação?
legacyExercises.explanation: Desculpe leads and a comma separates it from the question. The question itself is untouched.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the exchange and find the first direction the visitor is given.
legacyExercises.explanation: The first step is em frente, straight ahead, and the second comes after depois: à esquerda.
legacyExercises.passage:
Turista: Desculpe, onde fica a praia?
Moradora: Em frente, depois à esquerda.
Turista: Muito obrigado!
legacyExercises.translation:
Tourist: Excuse me, where is the beach?
Resident: Straight ahead, then to the left.
Tourist: Thank you very much!

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the Portuguese words in order to ask where the station is.
legacyExercises.explanation: Onde leads, fica follows because Portuguese asks where a place 'stays'. Estação is feminine, so its article is a.

lessons.culturalNote: Ouça and Desculpe both open a request in Portugal.

lessons.title: Prices and paying
lessons.objective: Ask what something costs, keep the price frame singular for one item, and hear why Portuguese orders with a softened verb.

legacyExercises.prompt: One of these lines will get a price out of a shopkeeper in Lisbon. Which one is it?
legacyExercises.explanation: Quanto custa? is the price question: quanto asks how much, and custa is the form of custar that fits one item.

legacyExercises.prompt: The meal is over and you want to pay in a Portuguese restaurant. Ask for the bill.
legacyExercises.explanation: Conta is feminine and takes a, and por favor carries the politeness on its own.

legacyExercises.prompt: You find the price reasonable and want to say as much. Negate «É caro.»
legacyExercises.explanation: Não goes ahead of the verb é, and the tilde on não is part of the word, never an optional flourish.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the blank in the question you would put to a stallholder: ___ custa o café?
legacyExercises.explanation: Quanto custa is the frame to memorise, and it stays singular while a single thing is being priced.

legacyExercises.prompt: At a pastelaria counter in Lisbon you want the price of one coffee. Ask it.
legacyExercises.explanation: Custa agrees with the one item, um café, so the question stays in the singular.

legacyExercises.prompt: A shop is asking a fortune for something small. Arrange the words into a sentence that calls it very expensive.
legacyExercises.explanation: Muito stands directly before caro, and isto is Portuguese's standalone 'this', the one used with no noun beside it.

lessons.culturalNote: In Portuguese cafés the bill usually arrives when you ask for it, so a conta, por favor ends the visit.

lessons.title: Days and times
lessons.objective: Count the Portuguese week from domingo and keep the hyphens that hold segunda-feira together.

legacyExercises.prompt: In Lisbon a shop sign swaps a single word at dawn. Choose today's word.
legacyExercises.explanation: Hoje is right. What is left over means the week, Monday and tomorrow.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the sentence before you write it. Monday is the second fair, so count from domingo: today is Monday.
legacyExercises.explanation: Hoje é plus the day. Domingo is the first feria, so Monday, the second, is segunda-feira.

legacyExercises.prompt: Give the English meaning: Na segunda-feira trabalho.
legacyExercises.explanation: Na marks on before a feminine weekday, and segunda-feira is the second fair.

legacyExercises.prompt: Portuguese counts the working days from domingo. Counting that way, which day is the fourth?
legacyExercises.explanation: Domingo is the first feria; segunda is second, terça third, so the fourth is quarta-feira.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the week. According to the passage, which day opens the week?
legacyExercises.explanation: The opening line names it: domingo é o primeiro dia da semana.
legacyExercises.passage: Domingo é o primeiro dia da semana. Na segunda-feira trabalho. Na terça-feira estudo português. Na quarta-feira descanso. Amanhã é quinta-feira.
legacyExercises.translation: Sunday is the first day of the week. On Monday I work. On Tuesday I study Portuguese. On Wednesday I rest. Tomorrow is Thursday.

legacyExercises.prompt: Build the Portuguese sentence for today is Wednesday, keeping the hyphen.
legacyExercises.explanation: Hoje first, then é, then the hyphenated day: quarta-feira.

legacyExercises.prompt: Complete with the noun for the morning, not the word for tomorrow: A ___ está fria.
legacyExercises.explanation: Manhã is the morning; amanhã, with an a in front, is tomorrow.

lessons.culturalNote: The numbered weekdays come from the church calendar, where Sunday was the first fair and Monday the second.

lessons.title: Family and people
lessons.objective: Introduce your relatives, and keep the small article Portuguese plants in front of a possessive.

legacyExercises.prompt: Portuguese marks the sister with a tilde. Which of these four words is she?
legacyExercises.explanation: The word for sister is irmã, tilde and all; strip its nasal sound and you get irmão, the brother. Pais is the parents, and família the family.

legacyExercises.prompt: Irmã is feminine. Which line says I have a sister with the article that matches her?
legacyExercises.explanation: Uma irmã is the feminine form; um irmã and uns irmã both mismatch the article to the noun.

legacyExercises.prompt: Change the sentence from one sister to two: Tenho uma irmã.
legacyExercises.explanation: The plural adds -s to irmã, and uma becomes duas: Tenho duas irmãs.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the family note. In which city did the parents stay?
legacyExercises.explanation: The brother and sister have moved on; the parents are the ones still in Lisbon.
legacyExercises.passage: Somos quatro em casa, mas só eu e a minha irmã vivemos no Porto. O meu irmão Max mudou-se para Coimbra no ano passado. Os meus pais ficaram em Lisboa, na casa antiga.
legacyExercises.translation: There are four of us at home, but only my sister and I live in Porto. My brother Max moved to Coimbra last year. My parents stayed in Lisbon, in the old house.

legacyExercises.prompt: Write the plural word for parents, article and all, into the gap: Os meus ___ vivem em Lisboa.
legacyExercises.explanation: Pais is plural and still keeps the article os alongside the possessive meus.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: I have a brother. (ter is irregular in the I form.)
legacyExercises.explanation: Ter is irregular, so the I form is tenho and not tene: Tenho um irmão.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order to say this is my family, keeping the article Portuguese wants.
legacyExercises.explanation: Portuguese keeps the article with the possessive, so the sentence is Esta é a minha família.

lessons.culturalNote: A família in Portuguese often includes grandparents and cousins, and it is the standard answer to tell me about yourself.

lessons.title: Build it: at the café
lessons.objective: Build café orders from blocks, keeping gostaria de and the thanks that matches the speaker.

lessons.title: Your mission: market day
lessons.objective: Complete your market list: ask prices, choose, and pay — all in Portuguese.

lessons.title: Look back: what you know
lessons.objective: Retrieve what eight lessons taught you — no new material, just memory.

lessons.title: Your mission: find the station
lessons.objective: Ask the way and follow directions to the station — all in Portuguese.

lessons.title: Your mission: check in
lessons.objective: Check in to a Lisbon hotel: greet, introduce yourself, ask the price, and pay — all in Portuguese.

lessons.title: Build it: my family
lessons.objective: Build sentences about your family from blocks — owners, agreements, and all.

lessons.title: Home and articles
lessons.objective: Name the rooms of a house and fuse em with the article: na cozinha, no quarto.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which word names the room where you cook?
legacyExercises.explanation: A cozinha is the kitchen — it carries the feminine article a, like a sala and a casa de banho.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence keeps the fused form Portuguese wants?
legacyExercises.explanation: Em + a fuses into na; splitting it (em a) or dropping it (em cozinha) both sound wrong.
options: O gato está em a cozinha.

legacyExercises.prompt: Change the room: O gato está no quarto. → The cat is in the kitchen.
legacyExercises.explanation: No becomes na for the feminine a cozinha: O gato está na cozinha.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the house note. Where does the cat sleep?
legacyExercises.explanation: The cat sleeps na sala — in the living room.
legacyExercises.passage: A minha casa tem três quartos. A cozinha é pequena, mas a sala é grande. O meu gato dorme na sala, e os livros estão no quarto.
legacyExercises.translation: My house has three bedrooms. The kitchen is small, but the living room is big. My cat sleeps in the living room, and the books are in the bedroom.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: A mesa está ___ sala. (in the living room)
legacyExercises.explanation: Em + a = na: A mesa está na sala.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: in the bedroom. (Remember what em + o becomes.)
legacyExercises.explanation: Em melts into o to make no: no quarto, in the bedroom.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: The books are in the bedroom.
legacyExercises.explanation: Os livros estão no quarto — note the plural os with the plural noun, and no doing its fused job.

lessons.culturalNote: Portuguese homes are often described room by room, and a casa usually means the whole flat or house, not just the building.

lessons.title: Describing things
lessons.objective: Describe people and things with adjectives that agree: alto/alta, novo/nova.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which adjective matches a sister? A minha irmã é ___.
legacyExercises.explanation: Alta matches the feminine irmã; alto would describe a brother.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
legacyExercises.explanation: Pequeno matches the masculine quarto; a cozinha would need pequena.

legacyExercises.prompt: Make it feminine: O meu irmão é alto. → My sister is tall.
legacyExercises.explanation: Both the noun and the adjective switch: A minha irmã é alta.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the house note. Which room is new?
legacyExercises.explanation: O meu quarto é novo — the bedroom is the new room.
legacyExercises.passage: A minha casa é antiga, mas é muito bonita. A cozinha é pequena e a sala é grande. O meu quarto é novo e muito confortável.
legacyExercises.translation: My house is old, but it is very pretty. The kitchen is small and the living room is big. My bedroom is new and very comfortable.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: A sala é ___ grande. (very)
legacyExercises.explanation: Muito never changes — it just turns the adjective up: muito grande.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: The house is new. (Casa is feminine.)
legacyExercises.explanation: Nova agrees with the feminine casa: A casa é nova.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: The coffee is very good.
legacyExercises.explanation: Muito sits in front of the adjective it boosts: O café é muito bom.

lessons.culturalNote: Portuguese compliments a home with nova and bonita the way English reaches for lovely — adjectives carry the warmth.

lessons.title: More than one
lessons.objective: Make plurals three ways: -s, -es, and the -ão rebels like pães.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which is the plural of o mês?
legacyExercises.explanation: Consonant endings take -es: o mês → os meses.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which phrase keeps everything plural?
legacyExercises.explanation: Article, noun and adjective all go plural: as casas grandes.

legacyExercises.prompt: Make it plural: A janela está aberta. → The windows are open.
legacyExercises.explanation: Everything shifts: as janelas estão abertas.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the bakery note. How many bread rolls does the writer buy?
legacyExercises.explanation: Dois pães — two bread rolls.
legacyExercises.passage: Na padaria compro dois pães e três croissants. Os pães são frescos e as janelas da padaria estão abertas. Gosto muito desta padaria.
legacyExercises.translation: At the bakery I buy two bread rolls and three croissants. The rolls are fresh and the bakery windows are open. I like this bakery a lot.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: Tenho ___ irmãos. (two)
legacyExercises.explanation: Dois matches the masculine irmãos; duas would pair with irmãs.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: the houses. (Casa is feminine.)
legacyExercises.explanation: Feminine plural article as with casas: as casas.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: I buy two bread rolls.
legacyExercises.explanation: The -ão rebel: pão → pães. Compro dois pães.

lessons.culturalNote: A padaria is a daily ritual in Portugal — pão fresco every morning, and the plural pães is one of the first irregulars you'll actually use.

lessons.title: Work and daily routine
lessons.objective: Talk about work and study with -ar verbs and time-of-day phrases.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which verb means to study?
legacyExercises.explanation: Estudar is to study — eu estudo, I study.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
legacyExercises.explanation: À tarde is the fixed block — never em a tarde or na tarde.

legacyExercises.prompt: Change the time: Trabalho de manhã. → I work in the afternoon.
legacyExercises.explanation: Swap the block: Trabalho à tarde.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the routine note. When does the writer study Portuguese?
legacyExercises.explanation: Estudo português à tarde — in the afternoon.
legacyExercises.passage: O meu dia é simples. Trabalho de manhã numa loja e estudo português à tarde. À noite janto em casa com a minha família. Gosto da minha rotina.
legacyExercises.translation: My day is simple. I work in the morning in a shop and study Portuguese in the afternoon. At night I have dinner at home with my family. I like my routine.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: Estudo português ___ manhã. (in the morning)
legacyExercises.explanation: De manhã is the fixed phrase — de, not em.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: I work in Lisbon. (-ar verbs swap -ar for -o.)
legacyExercises.explanation: Trabalhar → trabalho: Trabalho em Lisboa.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: I have dinner at home at night.
legacyExercises.explanation: The time block lands last: Janto em casa à noite.

lessons.culturalNote: The Portuguese day runs late — dinner at eight or nine is normal, and lunch is the big meal of the day.

lessons.title: Saying no
lessons.objective: Say no cleanly: não before the verb, and the emphatic doubles like não quero nada.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which word makes a verb negative?
legacyExercises.explanation: Não is the negator — it goes directly before the verb.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
legacyExercises.explanation: Não goes before the verb: Não falo português.

legacyExercises.prompt: Make it never: Como carne. → I never eat meat.
legacyExercises.explanation: Nunca replaces não for never: Nunca como carne.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the coffee note. What do they drink at home instead of coffee?
legacyExercises.explanation: Só chá — only tea.
legacyExercises.passage: Não gosto de café, nunca bebo café à noite. O meu irmão não bebe café, ele também não. Em casa não há café, só chá.
legacyExercises.translation: I don't like coffee, I never drink coffee at night. My brother doesn't drink coffee, he doesn't either. At home there is no coffee, only tea.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: Não está ___ em casa. (nobody)
legacyExercises.explanation: Ninguém pairs with não: Não está ninguém em casa.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: I don't speak Portuguese. (Não hugs the verb.)
legacyExercises.explanation: Não falo português — não sits right before falo.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: I don't want anything, thank you.
legacyExercises.explanation: The double negative is correct: Não quero nada, obrigado.

lessons.culturalNote: Ordering um descafeinado after dinner is perfectly normal in Portugal — nunca is a strong word, so não, obrigado usually suffices.

lessons.title: Asking questions
lessons.objective: Ask what, who, where, when and how — and soften it all with é que.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which word asks where?
legacyExercises.explanation: Onde asks where — Onde fica o hotel?

answers: Onde é que fica a estação?
legacyExercises.prompt: Which sounds the most naturally Portuguese?
legacyExercises.explanation: É que softens the question the Portuguese way: Onde é que fica a estação?
options: Onde é que fica a estação?
A estação fica onde é que?

legacyExercises.prompt: Ask about a person instead: O que é isto? → Who is she?
legacyExercises.explanation: Swap the question word: Quem é ela?

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the exchange. What does Miguel ask about second?
legacyExercises.explanation: Quando abre? — when it opens.
legacyExercises.passage: O Miguel pergunta: Onde é que fica a farmácia? A Ana responde: Fica na Rua Nova. O Miguel pergunta: Quando abre? A Ana responde: Abre às nove.
legacyExercises.translation: Miguel asks: Where is the pharmacy? Ana answers: It's on Rua Nova. Miguel asks: When does it open? Ana answers: It opens at nine.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: ___ estás? (how)
legacyExercises.explanation: Como asks how: Como estás?

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: What is this? (The question word is a pair.)
legacyExercises.explanation: O que is the pair — never just que here: O que é isto?

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: When do you arrive?
legacyExercises.explanation: Question word first, no reordering needed: Quando chegas?

lessons.culturalNote: É que is the great softener of Portuguese questions — it turns a demand into a conversation.

lessons.title: Food and drink
lessons.objective: Talk about eating and drinking: comer, beber, and gostar de.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which verb means to drink?
legacyExercises.explanation: Beber is to drink — eu bebo, I drink.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
legacyExercises.explanation: Gostar needs de: Gosto de peixe.

legacyExercises.prompt: Change the verb: Como sopa ao almoço. → I drink water.
legacyExercises.explanation: Beber → bebo: Bebo água.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the food note. What fruit does the writer eat every day?
legacyExercises.explanation: Uma maçã todos os dias — an apple every day.
legacyExercises.passage: Ao almoço como sopa e peixe. Bebo água e, às vezes, um sumo de laranja. Gosto muito de fruta, como uma maçã todos os dias. O jantar é leve.
legacyExercises.translation: At lunch I eat soup and fish. I drink water and, sometimes, an orange juice. I like fruit a lot, I eat an apple every day. Dinner is light.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: Gosto ___ fruta. (of)
legacyExercises.explanation: Gostar brings de along: Gosto de fruta.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: I eat soup at lunch. (-er verbs swap -er for -o.)
legacyExercises.explanation: Comer → como: Como sopa ao almoço.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: I drink an orange juice.
legacyExercises.explanation: Sumo is juice in Portugal: Bebo um sumo de laranja.

lessons.culturalNote: Sopa starts almost every Portuguese lunch, and peixe is a point of national pride — ask anyone.

lessons.title: Mine and yours
lessons.objective: Say what's yours: possessives that agree with the thing owned.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which possessive goes with casa? ___ casa é grande.
legacyExercises.explanation: Casa is feminine: a minha casa.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
legacyExercises.explanation: Article first, then the matching possessive: a minha casa.

legacyExercises.prompt: Change the owner: O meu carro é novo. → Your (informal) car is new.
legacyExercises.explanation: Teu is the informal your: O teu carro é novo.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the car note. Where are the keys?
legacyExercises.explanation: As minhas chaves estão na mala — in the bag.
legacyExercises.passage: O meu carro está na rua. A minha mala está no carro e as minhas chaves estão na mala. O teu carro está na garagem, é mais fácil.
legacyExercises.translation: My car is on the street. My bag is in the car and my keys are in the bag. Your car is in the garage, it's easier.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: ___ irmã vive no Porto. (my — feminine)
legacyExercises.explanation: A minha matches the feminine irmã.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: My friends live here. (Amigos is masculine plural.)
legacyExercises.explanation: Masculine plural needs os meus: Os meus amigos vivem aqui.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: My keys are here.
legacyExercises.explanation: Feminine plural all the way: As minhas chaves estão aqui.

lessons.culturalNote: O meu and a minha are said so often they blur into the noun — listen for the article and the possessive arrives with it.

lessons.title: Getting around
lessons.objective: Move around the city: ir, and de carro, de metro, a pé.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which phrase means on foot?
legacyExercises.explanation: A pé is on foot — the one transport without de.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
legacyExercises.explanation: Feet take a, not de: Vou a pé.

legacyExercises.prompt: Change how: Vou de carro. → I go by metro.
legacyExercises.explanation: Swap the transport: Vou de metro.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the commute note. How does the writer's sister travel?
legacyExercises.explanation: A minha irmã vai a pé — on foot.
legacyExercises.passage: Para ir ao centro, vou de metro. É rápido e barato. O meu amigo vai de carro, mas o trânsito é mau. A minha irmã vai a pé, ela vive perto.
legacyExercises.translation: To go downtown, I take the metro. It's fast and cheap. My friend goes by car, but the traffic is bad. My sister walks, she lives nearby.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: Vou ___ centro. (to the — a + o)
legacyExercises.explanation: A + o fuses into ao: Vou ao centro.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: I go downtown by metro. (Ir: eu vou.)
legacyExercises.explanation: Vou ao centro de metro — vou for I go, de metro for how.

answers: Ela vai para o trabalho a pé.
legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: She goes to work on foot.
legacyExercises.explanation: Ela vai para o trabalho a pé — destination with para, feet with a.

lessons.culturalNote: Lisboa's metro is clean, cheap and fast — de metro is often the smartest answer in the city.

lessons.title: Polite requests
lessons.objective: Ask politely: Pode…?, Gostaria de…, and the softening power of por favor.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which phrase means 'I would like…'?
legacyExercises.explanation: Gostaria de… is the polite I would like — softer than quero.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which is the most polite way to order a coffee?
legacyExercises.explanation: Queria (I wanted) softens the request — the classic polite order.

answers: Gostaria de um café, por favor.
legacyExercises.prompt: Make it polite: Quero um café. → I'd like a coffee, please.
legacyExercises.explanation: Queria or Gostaria de both soften quero.

answers: To book a table for two.
To book a table for two
legacyExercises.prompt: Read the restaurant exchange. What does the customer ask for first?
legacyExercises.explanation: Gostaria de reservar uma mesa para dois — a table for two.
legacyExercises.passage: No restaurante, o cliente diz: Com licença, gostaria de reservar uma mesa para dois. O empregado responde: Com certeza. É para hoje? Sim, para hoje às oito. Pode trazer a ementa, por favor?
legacyExercises.translation: At the restaurant, the customer says: Excuse me, I would like to book a table for two. The waiter answers: Of course. Is it for today? Yes, for today at eight. Can you bring the menu, please?

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: Pode ___-me, por favor? (help)
legacyExercises.explanation: Pode ajudar-me — the -me clitic glues to the verb.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: Can you help me, please? (Poder + -me on the verb.)
legacyExercises.explanation: Pode ajudar-me, por favor? — note -me glued after the verb, the European way.

answers: Com licença, onde fica a estação?
legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: Excuse me, where is the station?
legacyExercises.explanation: Com licença opens, onde asks: Com licença, onde fica a estação?

lessons.culturalNote: Com licença is the all-purpose Portuguese key — it opens conversations the way excuse me never quite does.

lessons.title: Yesterday: a first look at the past
lessons.objective: Tell finished stories: falei, comi, foi, fiz.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which form means 'I spoke'?
legacyExercises.explanation: Falei is the finished past: Ontem falei.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence is in the past?
legacyExercises.explanation: Comi is the pretérito perfeito — the finished action.

legacyExercises.prompt: Change the verb: Ontem falei com a Ana. → Yesterday I made dinner.
legacyExercises.explanation: Fazer is a rebel: fiz. Ontem fiz o jantar.

answers: Spoke with Ana at the café.
legacyExercises.prompt: Read the yesterday note. What did the writer do in the morning?
legacyExercises.explanation: De manhã falei com a Ana — spoke with Ana.
legacyExercises.passage: Ontem foi um dia ótimo. De manhã falei com a Ana no café. Ao almoço comi uma sopa muito boa. À tarde fiz compras e à noite vi um filme em casa.
legacyExercises.translation: Yesterday was a great day. In the morning I spoke with Ana at the café. At lunch I ate a very good soup. In the afternoon I went shopping and at night I watched a film at home.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: ___ um dia ótimo. (It was)
legacyExercises.explanation: Foi means it was here: Foi um dia ótimo.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: Yesterday I ate a soup. (Comer → comi.)
legacyExercises.explanation: Comer → comi: Ontem comi uma sopa.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: Yesterday I spoke with Ana.
legacyExercises.explanation: Ontem sets the time, falei tells the story.

lessons.culturalNote: Ontem is the storyteller's favorite word — start with it and any Portuguese speaker leans in.

lessons.title: Making plans
lessons.objective: Make plans the easy way: vou, vamos, and ir + infinitive.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which means 'let's' / 'we're going to'?
legacyExercises.explanation: Vamos covers we and let's: Vamos jantar fora?

legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
legacyExercises.explanation: Nothing goes between: vou comer.

legacyExercises.prompt: Change the plan: Amanhã vou estudar. → Next week I'm going to travel.
legacyExercises.explanation: Para a semana is next week: Para a semana vou viajar.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the plans note. Where is the writer going next week?
legacyExercises.explanation: Para a semana vamos viajar para o Algarve — to the Algarve.
legacyExercises.passage: Amanhã vou à praia de manhã. Depois vou almoçar com os meus amigos. Para a semana vamos viajar para o Algarve. Vai ser ótimo!
legacyExercises.translation: Tomorrow I'm going to the beach in the morning. Afterwards I'm going to have lunch with my friends. Next week we're going to travel to the Algarve. It's going to be great!

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: ___ chover à tarde. (It's going to rain)
legacyExercises.explanation: Vai chover — vai for it/he/she: Vai chover à tarde.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: Tomorrow I'm going to study. (Ir + infinitive.)
legacyExercises.explanation: Vou + estudar: Amanhã vou estudar.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: Shall we eat out?
legacyExercises.explanation: Vamos doubles as let's: Vamos jantar fora?

lessons.culturalNote: O Algarve is where Portugal goes on holiday — para a semana vamos is the sentence that starts a thousand trips.

lessons.title: Weather and seasons
lessons.objective: Talk about the sky and the seasons: Está sol, Faz calor, o verão.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which phrase means 'it's cloudy'?
legacyExercises.explanation: Está nublado — estar for the sky right now.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
legacyExercises.explanation: Faz calor — heat takes fazer.

legacyExercises.prompt: Change the season: O verão é quente. → Winter is cold.
legacyExercises.explanation: O inverno é frio — winter takes o.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the weather note. What is tomorrow going to be like?
legacyExercises.explanation: Amanhã vai estar nublado e vai chover — cloudy and rainy.
legacyExercises.passage: Hoje está sol e faz calor. É verão e gosto muito. Amanhã vai estar nublado e vai chover. No inverno faz frio, mas gosto do inverno também.
legacyExercises.translation: Today it's sunny and hot. It's summer and I like it a lot. Tomorrow it's going to be cloudy and rain. In winter it's cold, but I like winter too.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: Está ___ chover. (the European -ing: a)
legacyExercises.explanation: Está a chover is the European continuous: está + a + infinitive.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: It's sunny today. (Estar for the sky.)
legacyExercises.explanation: Está sol hoje — estar, not fazer.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: It's very hot in summer.
legacyExercises.explanation: Faz muito calor no verão.

lessons.culturalNote: Em Portugal, o verão is a serious affair — everything slows down in August and the conversation starts with Está calor.

lessons.title: Telling the time
lessons.objective: Tell the time: Que horas são? São três e meia.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which asks the time?
legacyExercises.explanation: Que horas são? — literally, what hours are they.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which is correct?
legacyExercises.explanation: É uma hora is the exception that proves the são rule.

legacyExercises.prompt: Change the time: São três e meia. → It's quarter to four.
legacyExercises.explanation: São quatro menos um quarto — menos subtracts.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the station note. When does the train leave?
legacyExercises.explanation: O comboio parte às quatro — at four.
legacyExercises.passage: Que horas são? São três e meia. O comboio parte às quatro. Temos tempo: vamos tomar um café. É meio-dia quando chegamos a Lisboa.
legacyExercises.translation: What time is it? It's half past three. The train leaves at four. We have time: let's have a coffee. It's midday when we arrive in Lisbon.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: ___ meio-dia. (It's)
legacyExercises.explanation: É meio-dia — noon takes é like one o'clock.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: It's one o'clock. (The famous exception.)
legacyExercises.explanation: É uma hora — one o'clock takes é, not são.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: It's half past three.
legacyExercises.explanation: São três e meia — e glues the half on.

lessons.culturalNote: Os comboios em Portugal usually run on time — às quatro means às quatro.

lessons.title: Months and dates
lessons.objective: Say months and dates: em junho, em 3 de maio.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which month is maio?
legacyExercises.explanation: Maio is May — em maio há flores.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which date is written correctly?
legacyExercises.explanation: Em 3 de maio — day, de, lowercase month.

legacyExercises.prompt: Change the month: Em janeiro faz frio. → In May there are flowers.
legacyExercises.explanation: Em maio há flores.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the birthday note. When is the party?
legacyExercises.explanation: Em 15 de junho — on June 15th.
legacyExercises.passage: O meu aniversário é em junho, no dia 15. A festa é em 15 de junho em minha casa. Em maio preparo tudo. O ano passado foi muito divertido.
legacyExercises.translation: My birthday is in June, on the 15th. The party is on June 15th at my house. In May I prepare everything. Last year was a lot of fun.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: O ano tem doze ___. (months)
legacyExercises.explanation: O ano tem doze meses.

answers: O meu aniversário é em junho.
legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: My birthday is in June. (Months are lowercase.)
legacyExercises.explanation: O meu aniversário é em junho — junho stays lowercase.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: I arrive on May 3rd.
legacyExercises.explanation: Chego em 3 de maio.

lessons.culturalNote: Santos Populares fill June with parties in Lisbon — saying o meu aniversário é em junho usually earns an invitation.

lessons.title: At the market
lessons.objective: Shop by quantity: um quilo de, uma garrafa de, uma dúzia de.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which means 'a dozen'?
legacyExercises.explanation: Uma dúzia de ovos — a dozen eggs.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which is correct?
legacyExercises.explanation: De bridges amount and goods: um quilo de maçãs.

legacyExercises.prompt: Change the amount: Um quilo de maçãs. → Half a kilo of cheese.
legacyExercises.explanation: Meio quilo de queijo.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the market note. What does the writer buy besides apples, cheese and eggs?
legacyExercises.explanation: Uma garrafa de água — a bottle of water.
legacyExercises.passage: No mercado compro um quilo de maçãs e meio quilo de queijo. Peço também uma dúzia de ovos. O peixe é fresco hoje. Também levo uma garrafa de água.
legacyExercises.translation: At the market I buy a kilo of apples and half a kilo of cheese. I also ask for a dozen eggs. The fish is fresh today. I'll also take a bottle of water.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: O peixe é ___? (fresh)
legacyExercises.explanation: É fresco? — the market's quality check.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: I'd like a kilo of apples. (Amount + de + goods.)
legacyExercises.explanation: Queria um quilo de maçãs — don't skip the de.

answers: Uma garrafa de água, por favor.
legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: A bottle of water, please.
legacyExercises.explanation: Uma garrafa de água, por favor.

lessons.culturalNote: O mercado is a morning affair — go early, ask É fresco?, and never squeeze the fruit before asking.

lessons.title: Free time and hobbies
lessons.objective: Talk about hobbies: Gosto de…, jogar, ouvir música.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which verb goes with futebol?
legacyExercises.explanation: Jogar futebol — jogar is for sports with rules.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which is correct?
legacyExercises.explanation: Gostar always brings de.

legacyExercises.prompt: Change the hobby: Gosto de ler. → I like to swim.
legacyExercises.explanation: Gosto de nadar — infinitive after de.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the weekend note. What does the writer's brother like to do?
legacyExercises.explanation: O meu irmão gosta de cozinhar — to cook.
legacyExercises.passage: No fim de semana gosto de descansar. Jogo futebol aos sábados com os meus amigos. Ouço música todos os dias e leio muito à noite. O meu irmão gosta de cozinhar.
legacyExercises.translation: On the weekend I like to rest. I play football on Saturdays with my friends. I listen to music every day and read a lot at night. My brother likes to cook.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: Jogo futebol ___ sábados. (on — aos)
legacyExercises.explanation: Aos sábados — on Saturdays.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: I like reading. (Gostar de + infinitive.)
legacyExercises.explanation: Gosto de ler — de plus the infinitive.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: I listen to music every day.
legacyExercises.explanation: Ouço música todos os dias.

lessons.culturalNote: Futebol is closer to religion than hobby in Portugal — saying jogo futebol opens more doors than any grammar.

lessons.title: Health and the body
lessons.objective: Talk about pain and illness: Dói-me…, Estou doente, Tenho febre.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which means 'my head hurts'?
legacyExercises.explanation: Dói-me a cabeça — the verb doer with -me.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which is correct?
legacyExercises.explanation: The article stays, -me glues after the verb: Dói-me a cabeça.

legacyExercises.prompt: Change the symptom: Tenho febre. → I'm sick.
legacyExercises.explanation: Estar for states: Estou doente.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the sick note. When is the writer going to the doctor?
legacyExercises.explanation: Amanhã vou ao médico de manhã — tomorrow morning.
legacyExercises.passage: Hoje estou doente. Dói-me a cabeça e tenho febre. Não vou trabalhar. Amanhã vou ao médico de manhã. Espero melhorar depressa.
legacyExercises.translation: Today I'm sick. My head hurts and I have a fever. I'm not going to work. Tomorrow I'm going to the doctor in the morning. I hope to get better soon.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: Dói-me ___ cabeça. (the — feminine)
legacyExercises.explanation: Dói-me a cabeça — the article is required.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: My arm hurts. (Dói-me + article + part.)
legacyExercises.explanation: Dói-me o braço — masculine o for o braço.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: I'm going to the doctor.
legacyExercises.explanation: Vou ao médico — a + o fuses into ao.

lessons.culturalNote: Em Portugal diz-se Estou constipado for a cold — and the farmácia is the first stop, not the doctor.

lessons.title: At the pharmacy
lessons.objective: Get what you need: Preciso de…, para a dor de cabeça.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which verb means 'to need'?
legacyExercises.explanation: Precisar de — Preciso de aspirina.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which is correct?
legacyExercises.explanation: Precisar + de, always.

answers: Preciso de um xarope para a tosse.
legacyExercises.prompt: Change the need: Preciso de aspirina. → I need a syrup for the cough.
legacyExercises.explanation: Preciso de um xarope para a tosse.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the pharmacy note. What does the pharmacist ask for?
legacyExercises.explanation: Tem receita? — do you have a prescription.
legacyExercises.passage: Na farmácia digo: Bom dia, preciso de aspirina. É para a dor de cabeça. A farmacêutica pergunta: Tem receita? Não preciso, é só para a dor. Ela dá-me o xarope e a aspirina.
legacyExercises.translation: At the pharmacy I say: Good morning, I need aspirin. It's for the headache. The pharmacist asks: Do you have a prescription? I don't need one, it's just for the pain. She gives me the syrup and the aspirin.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: Tem alguma coisa ___ a tosse? (for)
legacyExercises.explanation: Para a tosse — para says what it's for.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: I need aspirin. (Precisar brings de.)
legacyExercises.explanation: Preciso de aspirina — never skip the de.

answers: É para a dor de cabeça.
legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: It's for the headache.
legacyExercises.explanation: É para a dor de cabeça — para for purpose, de for possession.

lessons.culturalNote: A farmácia de serviço stays open all night on rotation — look for the green cross, a cruz verde.

lessons.title: Emergencies
lessons.objective: Handle the worst: Socorro!, Chame…!, and É urgente!

legacyExercises.prompt: Which word cries for help?
legacyExercises.explanation: Socorro! — the word that needs no grammar.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which is the correct emergency command?
legacyExercises.explanation: Chame with -e addresses strangers — the safe default.

legacyExercises.prompt: Change who to call: Chame uma ambulância! → Call the police!
legacyExercises.explanation: Chame a polícia!

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the emergency note. What does the man shout first?
legacyExercises.explanation: Socorro! — help!
legacyExercises.passage: Há um acidente na rua. Um homem grita: Socorro! Chame uma ambulância! É urgente! Uma mulher pergunta: Onde fica o hospital?
legacyExercises.translation: There's an accident on the street. A man shouts: Help! Call an ambulance! It's urgent! A woman asks: Where is the hospital?

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: É ___! (urgent)
legacyExercises.explanation: É urgente! — when seconds matter.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: Call an ambulance! (Imperative: Chame…)
legacyExercises.explanation: Chame uma ambulância! — the -e ending for strangers.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: Where is the hospital?
legacyExercises.explanation: Onde fica o hospital?

lessons.culturalNote: 112 is the European emergency number — one number for ambulância, polícia and bombeiros.

lessons.title: Invitations
lessons.objective: Invite, accept and decline kindly: Queres vir…?, com prazer, desta vez não.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which accepts warmly?
legacyExercises.explanation: Sim, com prazer! — yes, with pleasure.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which declines kindly?
legacyExercises.explanation: Desta vez não posso, desculpa — cushioned, not cold.

legacyExercises.prompt: Soften the invitation: Queres vir jantar? → Would you like to come to the cinema?
legacyExercises.explanation: Gostavas de…? — the conditional softens beautifully.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read the invitation. When is the dinner?
legacyExercises.explanation: Sábado, às oito — Saturday at eight.
legacyExercises.passage: A Ana convida o Miguel: Queres vir jantar no sábado? O Miguel responde: Sim, com prazer! A que horas? Às oito, em minha casa. Obrigado pelo convite, diz o Miguel.
legacyExercises.translation: Ana invites Miguel: Do you want to come for dinner on Saturday? Miguel answers: Yes, with pleasure! At what time? At eight, at my house. Thanks for the invitation, says Miguel.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: Sim, ___ prazer! (with)
legacyExercises.explanation: Com prazer — with pleasure.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: Do you want to come for dinner? (Queres vir…?)
legacyExercises.explanation: Queres vir jantar? — the classic invitation.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: Thanks for the invitation.
legacyExercises.explanation: Obrigado pelo convite — por + o fuses into pelo.

lessons.culturalNote: A dinner invitation in Portugal means arrive a touch late and stay long — leaving early is the real faux pas.

lessons.title: O pretérito perfeito
lessons.objective: Form the pretérito perfeito of regular verbs: falei, comeste, partiu, falámos.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which means 'I spoke yesterday'?
legacyExercises.explanation: Falei ontem — falei is the pretérito perfeito of falar (-ei ending). Falo is present, falava is the imperfeito, and falar is the infinitive.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form before you write it: you (tu) ate, yesterday — '___ o bolo todo?' (Did you eat the whole cake?)
legacyExercises.explanation: Comeste o bolo todo? — -er verbs take -este for tu in the perfeito: comeste.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which verb is irregular in the pretérito perfeito?
legacyExercises.explanation: Fiz — fazer becomes fiz, an irregular. Falei, comi and partiu are all regular formations.

legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: I had dinner at home yesterday.
legacyExercises.explanation: Ontem jantei em casa — time word first is the natural Portuguese habit.

legacyExercises.prompt: Say: We bought bread this morning.
legacyExercises.explanation: Comprámos pão de manhã — nós form of comprar in the perfeito is comprámos, with the accent.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: Ela ___ às oito. (she left)
legacyExercises.explanation: Partiu — ela form of partir in the perfeito: -iu ending.

answers: She ate a sandwich and left for work.
She ate a sandwich and left for work at two.
Comeu uma sandes e partiu para o trabalho.
legacyExercises.prompt: Read about yesterday. What did she do in the afternoon?
legacyExercises.explanation: She ate a sandwich and left for work at two — 'comi uma sandes e parti para o trabalho às duas'.
legacyExercises.passage: Ontem foi um dia fixe. De manhã, falei com a Ana ao telemóvel. À tarde, comi uma sandes e parti para o trabalho às duas. À noite, jantei em casa e vi um filme.
legacyExercises.translation: Yesterday was a great day. In the morning I spoke to Ana on the phone. In the afternoon I ate a sandwich and left for work at two. In the evening I had dinner at home and watched a film.

lessons.culturalNote: Portuguese people love a good story about yesterday — ontem fiz isto, ontem fiz aquilo. The pretérito perfeito is the engine of every anecdote at the café table.

lessons.title: O imperfeito
lessons.objective: Form the imperfeito for habits and descriptions: falava, comia, era, costumava.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which describes a habit in the past?
legacyExercises.explanation: Brincava na rua — the -ava ending marks the imperfeito: used to play. Brinquei is one completed event, brinco is present.

legacyExercises.prompt: Predict the form: he used to eat at seven — 'Ele ___ sempre às sete.'
legacyExercises.explanation: Ele comia sempre às sete — -er verbs take -ia in the imperfeito: comia.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which verb is irregular in the imperfeito?
legacyExercises.explanation: Era — ser becomes era, one of only three irregulars (era, tinha, vinha). Falava, comia and partia are regular.

answers: Quando era criança, brincava na rua.
legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: When I was a child I used to play in the street.
legacyExercises.explanation: Quando era criança, brincava na rua — the quando clause sets the scene, then the habit.

legacyExercises.prompt: Say: We were watching TV.
legacyExercises.explanation: Estávamos a ver televisão — the very Portuguese past progressive: estar in the imperfeito + a + infinitivo.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: Ele ___ sempre às sete. (he used to eat)
legacyExercises.explanation: Comia — imperfeito of comer for ele: -ia ending.

legacyExercises.prompt: Read about Tiago's childhood. How did he get to school?
legacyExercises.explanation: He walked — 'ia a pé para a escola'.
legacyExercises.passage: Quando era pequeno, o Tiago vivia numa aldeia. Acordava cedo, tomava o pequeno-almoço com a avó e ia a pé para a escola. À tarde, brincava com os amigos até às seis.
legacyExercises.translation: When he was little, Tiago lived in a village. He used to wake up early, have breakfast with his grandmother and walk to school. In the afternoon he used to play with his friends until six.

lessons.culturalNote: Quando era criança… (When I was a child…) opens a thousand Portuguese conversations. The imperfeito is the tense of nostalgia — childhood streets, grandmother's kitchen, summers that never ended.

lessons.title: Perfeito ou imperfeito?
lessons.objective: Choose between perfeito and imperfeito: completed events vs background and habits.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which sentence mixes background and event correctly?
legacyExercises.explanation: Estava a chover quando cheguei — imperfeito sets the scene (was raining), perfeito is the event (arrived). The other options pair two backgrounds or two events.
options: Estava a chover quando estava a chegar.

answers: Enquanto ela cozinhava, ele pôs a mesa.
legacyExercises.prompt: Complete the background: 'Enquanto ela ___, ele pôs a mesa.' (she was cooking)
legacyExercises.explanation: Enquanto ela cozinhava — enquanto signals ongoing background, so the imperfeito: cozinhava.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which word signals a one-time completed event?
legacyExercises.explanation: De repente — suddenly marks a single finished event, so it pairs with the perfeito. Todos os dias, sempre and enquanto signal habits or background.

answers: Todos os dias ia ao café.
legacyExercises.prompt: Put the words in order: I used to go to the café every day.
legacyExercises.explanation: Todos os dias ia ao café — the frequency phrase leads, then the habitual imperfeito.

legacyExercises.prompt: Say: Suddenly the phone rang.
legacyExercises.explanation: De repente, o telemóvel tocou — de repente + perfeito: tocar → tocou.

legacyExercises.prompt: Fill the gap: ___ a chover quando cheguei. (it was)
legacyExercises.explanation: Estava — the background weather takes the imperfeito: estava a chover.

answers: He was reading at the café.
legacyExercises.prompt: Read about Saturday. What was he doing when his friend arrived?
legacyExercises.explanation: He was reading at the café — 'Eu estava a ler no café quando o meu amigo chegou.'
legacyExercises.passage: Sábado foi um dia estranho. Estava a fazer sol de manhã, mas de repente começou a chover. Eu estava a ler no café quando o meu amigo chegou. Todos os dias ele vai ao café às três, mas no sábado chegou às cinco.
legacyExercises.translation: Saturday was a strange day. It was sunny in the morning, but suddenly it started to rain. I was reading at the café when my friend arrived. Every day he goes to the café at three, but on Saturday he arrived at five.

lessons.culturalNote: Portuguese storytelling weaves the two pasts together: the imperfeito sets the scene (estava a chover…), the perfeito drops the event (…quando cheguei). Master the weave and your anecdotes sound native.

lessons.title: Contar o fim de semana
lessons.objective: Narrate your weekend with sequencers: no sábado, depois, então, à noite.

answers: De manhã fui ao mercado, depois almocei, à noite vi um filme.
legacyExercises.prompt: Which orders the day correctly, morning to night?
legacyExercises.explanation: De manhã fui ao mercado, depois almocei, à noite vi um filme — time markers in chronological order with perfeitos. The others scramble the day or mix tenses.
options: De manhã fui ao mercado, depois almocei, à noite vi um filme.
